Background: Revenue at frontier AI companies has grown rapidly over the last few years. AI Digest’s [AI 2025 Forecasting Survey](https://ai2025.org/) [asked](https://theaidigest.org/ai2025-analysis-may#7-what-will-be-the-sum-of-openai-anthropic-and-xais-publicly-reported-annualized-revenues-by-december-31st-2025-in-usd-billions) forecasters to predict the combined annualized revenue of OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI by the end of 2025; the median forecast was $16 billion, but the [resolved](https://theaidigest.org/2025-forecast-results#ais-prominence-underestimated-revenue-and-overestimated-public-perception) value ended up being more than $30 billion. Growth has continued into 2026, and revenue is now one of the most closely watched indicators of whether frontier AI is generating real economic returns or whether high valuations are disconnected from underlying unit economics. Note that we exclude xAI from our version. 
A note on the revenue metric: both companies headline an "annualized revenue run-rate" rather than audited Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) figures, but they compute it differently. This question uses each company's headline run-rate as reported; see resolution criteria for part b for details.

Resolution Criteria: 
- This question will resolve using the most recently publicly reported annualized revenue run-rate for each of OpenAI and Anthropic as of December 31 of each resolution year, as that company reports it, as disclosed by the companies themselves via statements or official/company-leadership social media, or reported by reputable financial media (e.g. Bloomberg, Reuters, The Wall Street Journal, The Information). Figures are taken as headline-reported. FRI will not normalize for differences in annualization convention or accounting basis (e.g., gross vs. net) between the companies. Where a company materially restates its revenue definition, FRI will convene a panel of qualified experts to determine a comparable figure.
- If no reliable figure has been published within 12 months of a resolution date or if there is substantial variance among similarly reliable sources, FRI will convene a panel of qualified experts to estimate the figure using available evidence.
- If either company ceases to exist as an independent company  (per definition in 1.a.), the resolution value will include only the remaining company. If one of these companies acquires the other, the resolution will be its annualized revenue run-rate.

The companion question (1.a.) defines "exists as an independent company": Resolution Criteria: “Exists as an independent company” means that it has not failed, been acquired by another entity, or been nationalized. 1. Failure. The company has been dissolved or liquidated or has filed for, or been placed into, liquidation proceedings (e.g., Chapter 7 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code or equivalent). Also includes cases where the company has permanently ceased its principal business operations. A reorganization under Chapter 11 (or equivalent) does not count as failure so long as the company emerges or proceedings are ongoing on the resolution date. 2. Acquisition / loss of independence. Generally applies when a new entity obtains greater than 50% of voting securities. This might include mergers where the company is not the surviving entity or where a new entity obtains the contractual right to appoint a majority of the board. An IPO would not automatically constitute ceasing to exist as an independent company. An IPO would only trigger this condition if it led to a single entity acquiring greater than 50% of voting securities/contractual right to appoint a majority of the board. 3. Nationalization. Includes acquisition (by the above definition) by a government. Also includes cases where a government has placed the company into conservatorship, receivership, or equivalent state control (e.g., Fannie Mae/AIG). Golden shares, Defense Production Act orders, security agreements, or board observers would not count as nationalization. Changes in corporate form, renaming, or internal restructuring does not affect resolution, provided a clear successor entity continues the company's principal business independently. If OpenAI and Anthropic merge with each other, they will still “exist as an independent company” for purposes of this question.

For each condition below, assume that the year in which more than 50% of the LEAP panel first agrees that Expert AGI, as defined above, exists takes the stated value. Wave 8: Timelines (fielded 2026-04-20 to 2026-05-11) asks, first: What is the probability that, before 2100, more than 50% of LEAP panelists will agree that AGI exists, and if it occurs, in what year do you expect this to first occur? And then: Assume that more than 50% of LEAP panelists agree that AGI exists by the above definition before 2100. In what year do you expect this to first occur?

Background: Experts agree that knowing when AI will be able to perform on the same level as humans in most or all fields is important, but there is much less consensus on how to define an AI that reaches that milestone. Here, we offer one potential definition of AGI focused on AI systems’ ability to replace all but the best humans at nearly all non-physical tasks that generate economic value and are paid for in today’s labor market.

Resolution Criteria: Ground Truth. FRI - LEAP Panel

- “Professional employee” refers to a trained or experienced worker. To satisfy this question’s criteria, a system must perform at or above the level of the 90th percentile of such human workers in 2025, across all sectors. To qualify, the system should be able to replace individual human employees with the same level of support and supervision required for a 90th percentile human in the occupation in 2025.
- “Economically useful non-physical occupation” refers to work for which there is a paying market and where the worker’s value-add is dominated by cognitive rather than physical skills.
    - These occupations are dominated by analytical and creative tasks such as reasoning, planning, learning new information, communication, and decision-making.
    - For the purposes of this question, roles that are in-scope include: doctors and nurses, lawyers and legal aids, project managers, and AI/robotics researchers.
    - Roles that are out-of-scope include construction laborers, police officers, factory line workers, professional athletes, and electricians.
    - You should consider these roles as they existed at the end of 2025, even if you expect future versions of them to involve human-AI interaction to a much greater degree than they do currently.
    - To satisfy this question’s criteria, a system must outperform the 90th percentile 2025 human on at least 90% of the non-physical tasks associated with the role.
- The system must be commercially available, general, and no more than 5x as costly as equivalent human labor.
    - A system is considered “commercially available” if it can be purchased or licensed by firms or individuals (or is freely available), rather than being restricted to internal research use.
    - The system must be general - i.e., a single system that can reach the required level of performance across all relevant occupations.
    - To qualify, the AI's inference cost for replacing the labor of a given human professional must be within 5x of the equivalent human labor cost. For example, the AI inference cost necessary to replace a human’s yearly output must be no more than 5x their salary.
- This question will be resolved by FRI surveying the LEAP panel, or another expert panel with similar representation as LEAP.
    - We will ask them the following question and include the same definitions as provided above: “Imagine occupations as they were in 2025, focused on those whose economic value-add was primarily non-physical. Thinking of today’s AI systems, is there a commercially available system that could have performed as well or better than the 90th percentile professional employee in those 2025 occupations at no more than 5x the cost?” 
    - The LEAP panel estimate is computed by weighting the four expert categories (computer science, AI industry, economics, policy) equally, and then adjusting for demographic characteristics within each category. If the LEAP panel is not available by the resolution date, FRI will recruit a similar expert panel to resolve the question.

Definitions. ECI: the Epoch Capabilities Index, published by Epoch AI -- a single score summarising a model's results across dozens of benchmarks, fit with an item-response model so that scores stay comparable as benchmarks saturate and new ones are added.
